source_credit: Jeff Bezos: Amazon shareholder letters 1997 to 2020. Plain one-line maxims in our own words.

entries.text: Run the business like you just opened. Getting too comfortable is how a business declines.
Keep trying new things and accept that some will fail. Do more of what customers love.
Decide with about 70 percent of the facts. Waiting for more usually costs you.
For choices you cannot undo, slow down. Get advice and think it through.
Most choices can be undone. Make them fast and fix them if they go wrong.
Let trusted crew make small calls fast. Save slow, careful debate for the big ones.
If you cannot explain a plan in plain words, write it out until you can.
Put the customer first, try new ideas, and be patient. Stick with those for years.
Watch your customers more than your rivals. Customer focus protects a business best.
Customers always want something better, even when they say they are happy. Keep improving for them.
New ideas draw criticism at first. If you believe in one, stay with it.
Be firm on your goal and flexible on how you get there.
New ideas come with failed tries. Accept small failures as the cost of learning.
Take a few long shots with big upside. Expect most of them to miss.
In business, one big win can pay for many small misses. Keep trying.
Picture yourself at 80. You will regret what you never tried more than failing.
Most regrets come from chances you skipped. When unsure, ask what you will regret later.
When people disagree with your call, ask them to back it anyway. Then everyone commits fully.
Sometimes you should back your team's call even when you disagree.
When people truly want different things, settle it fast. Otherwise the most stubborn person wins.
Keep your standards high. Good people want to work where standards are high.
Tell new hires what good work looks like and how long it takes to learn.
When a customer's story does not match your numbers, check the numbers first.
Do not just promise to do better. Set up a step that stops the mistake.
Keep teams small. Small teams move faster and know who owns what.
Start with what the customer needs. Then learn the skills to deliver it.
Before you start something new, write the announcement. If it sounds dull, do not build it.
Run more small tests each year. More tries means more wins, even if most fail.
Watch cash coming in more than paper profit. Cash is what you can actually use.
Judge success by the value you build over many years, not this month.
If you must choose between looking good on paper and real future cash, take the cash.
